content: The study compares the use of anakinra versus standard of care (SOC) in the treatment of COVID-19 through a randomized controlled trial (RCT). The following outcomes were analyzed using forest plots: 1. All-cause mortality: A forest plot was generated to compare the effect of anakinra versus usual care on overall mortality rates among COVID-19 patients. 2. Discharge from hospital at day 28: The analysis assessed the proportion of patients discharged from the hospital by day 28 in the anakinra group compared to the usual care group. 3. Time to hospital discharge: The time, measured in days, until hospital discharge was compared between patients receiving anakinra and those receiving usual care. 4. Clinical improvement: The study evaluated clinical improvement outcomes in patients treated with anakinra versus those receiving standard care. 5. ICU admission: The likelihood of requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) was compared between the two groups. 6. Length of ICU stay: The duration of ICU stay was analyzed for patients treated with anakinra versus those receiving usual care. 7. Discharge from ICU at day 28: The proportion of patients discharged from the ICU by day 28 was compared between the anakinra and usual care groups. 8. Mechanical ventilation: The need for mechanical ventilation was assessed in patients treated with anakinra versus those receiving standard care. 9. Non-invasive ventilation: The requirement for non-invasive ventilation was compared between the two groups. 10. Serious adverse events: The incidence of serious adverse events was analyzed to evaluate the safety profile of anakinra compared to usual care. These outcomes were visualized and analyzed using Review Manager (RevMan) version 5.4.1.
